Most requested

Frameless Shower Doors

Heavy 3/8″ or 1/2″ glass with minimal clips and hinges. The clean, spa look that makes tile the star and a small bath feel bigger.

Typical range $1,200 – $3,800 installed*

Semi-Frameless Doors

Frameless door panel with slim framing only where structure needs it. A smart middle ground — modern look, friendlier budget.

Typical range $850 – $1,900 installed*

Framed Enclosures

Fully framed glass for guest baths, rentals, and budget remodels. Sturdy, water-tight, and available in fast-turn standard sizes.

Typical range $600 – $1,300 installed*

Sliding & Barn-Style Doors

Top-rolling barn hardware or classic bypass sliders for tight baths where a swinging door would hit a vanity or toilet.

Typical range $1,400 – $2,900 installed*

Tub Enclosures

Sliding or swinging glass over a tub — ditch the curtain, keep splash in, and make a tub/shower combo look intentional.

Typical range $700 – $1,600 installed*

Steam Showers

Floor-to-ceiling glass with sealed edges and a transom or operable vent panel, templated for steam generators.

Typical range $2,800 – $5,500 installed*

Corner & Neo-Angle

90° corner and neo-angle enclosures for compact primary baths — maximizes shower footprint without moving plumbing.

Typical range $2,200 – $4,200 installed*

Glass Replacement & Repair

Cracked panel, failed seal, dragging door, or worn rollers? We replace single panels, sweeps, seals, and hardware.

Turn This Into a Real Quote

How it works — 4 steps, no surprises

Most hold-ups in shower glass come from bad measuring. Our whole process is built around one precise template.

1

Ballpark first

Share a photo link + rough width in the form and send it — it comes straight to us. Get a planning range by reply before anyone comes to your house.

2

Free measure & template

We visit, laser-measure, check walls for plumb, and confirm glass, finish, and swing/slide direction with you.

3

Fabrication

Glass is cut, polished, drilled, and tempered to your template. Tempered glass can't be trimmed later — which is why step 2 matters.

4

Install & walkthrough

Most installs take 1.5–3 hours. We seal, align, test the sweep, and show you how to care for the coating and seals.

Frameless vs. framed — which should you pick?

  • Pick frameless if this is your forever bath, you love your tile, or you want the room to feel larger.
  • Pick semi-frameless if you want the look but need to hold budget for tile or fixtures.
  • Pick framed for rentals, guest baths, or the tightest timelines.

What to have ready for the measure

  • Tile and curb fully finished — glass is templated to finished surfaces
  • Fixture finish picked (so hardware matches on day one)
  • Door swing path clear — check vanity & toilet clearance
  • Any inspiration photo you love — it helps more than measurements alone

After you approve the written quote, glass is fabricated to your template — custom tempered glass typically takes 1–3 weeks to be ready — and install itself is usually one visit of 1.5–3 hours. Frameless doors aren't sealed like a framed door — they use sweeps and seals with small gaps by design. With a properly sloped curb and correct shower-head placement, water stays in. We'll flag any curb or spray issue at the measure, before you spend anything.
Both are tempered safety glass. 1/2″ feels more substantial, flexes less on wide doors, and costs more. 3/8″ is the workhorse for most doors and panels. For very wide or tall doors we may recommend 1/2″ — we'll explain why on your quote if so.
Often, yes — if the hardware and remaining panels are sound. Paste photo links in the quote form (choose “Glass replacement / repair”). Tempered glass can't be cut down, so a replacement panel is fabricated to match.
Yes — for a custom fit, tile, curb, and walls must be in their final finished state before templating. Measuring over unfinished walls is how gaps and leaks happen.
